newsitem.title: CANADA: CARGILL PEGS CANADA CANOLA OUTPUT AT 6.0-6.2 MLN T.
newsitem.headline: CARGILL PEGS CANADA CANOLA OUTPUT AT 6.0-6.2 MLN T.

text.p: The president of Cargill Ltd said the company expects Canadian canola production in the 6.0 to 6.2 million tonne range for the current crop year, below recent government estimates due to the effects of dry weather.
"Yields have come down since Agriculture Canada's forecast because of drought stress," Cargill Ltd president Kerry Hawkins said in an interview.

Agriculture Canada on August 5 forecast Canadian canola production in 1997/98 (Aug/July) to reach 6.24 million tonnes. Canada produced 5.0 million tonnes of canola in 1996/97 on 3.45 million hectares (8.525 million acres), Statistics Canada figures show.

Statistics Canada reported on June 27 that 12.025 million acres were seeded to canola and Agriculture Canada on August 5 forecast 4.779 million hectares (11.81 million acres) of canola would be harvested.
South Alberta, most of Saskatchewan and southwest Manitoba received little rain through July and early August and have reported drought conditions.
"It's a shortfall, but a heck of a lot better than last year," Hawkins added.
Canadian farmers seeded 8.685 million acres to canola in 1996/97 and produced 5.0 million tonnes, StatsCan said.
